⚡_CRITICAL_RULES_READ_FIRST.⭐_importance: These rules are NON-NEGOTIABLE and prevent 90% of porting issues

1_USE_NATIVE_RUST_RESULT.rule: DO NOT create custom Result<T,E> wrapper - USE RUST'S BUILT-IN
1_USE_NATIVE_RUST_RESULT.reason: Rust's Result IS what the C# Result was modeled after
1_USE_NATIVE_RUST_RESULT.wrong: pub struct Result<T, E> { /* custom wrapper */ }

usage.propagate: let value = might_fail()?; // Auto-return Err if failed

2_USE_NATIVE_RUST_COLLECTIONS.rule: DO NOT use DixCore wrappers - USE RUST'S BUILT-IN COLLECTIONS + ITERTOOLS
2_USE_NATIVE_RUST_COLLECTIONS.reason: Native Rust collections are zero-cost, well-tested, and idiomatic
2_USE_NATIVE_RUST_COLLECTIONS.decision: DixCore wrappers removed - too much trait bound complexity for minimal benefit

3_BORROWING_RULES.rule: You can have EITHER many readers OR one writer, NEVER both
3_BORROWING_RULES.the_golden_rule: Aliasing XOR Mutability - many reads OR one write, not both

mutable_borrows.can_have: ONLY ONE mutable borrow at a time
mutable_borrows.cannot_do: Have other borrows (even immutable) while mutable exists

common_error.wrong:
let r1 = &mut data;
let r2 = &mut data; // ERROR!

lifetime_basics.what: References must NEVER outlive the data they point to
lifetime_basics.example: fn longest<'a>(s1: &'a str, s2: &'a str) -> &'a str
lifetime_basics.meaning: Output lives as long as BOTH inputs (shortest lifetime)

4_OWNERSHIP_RULES.rule: Each value has EXACTLY ONE owner. When owner drops, value is freed.

1_move.example:
let s1 = String::from("hello");
let s2 = s1; // s1 MOVED, can't use anymore
1_move.when: Passing to function that consumes it

2_borrow.when: Function needs to READ but not own

3_clone.what: Deep copy - creates NEW owned value
3_clone.example: let s2 = s1.clone(); // Both valid, but expensive
3_clone.when: ONLY when you actually need TWO independent copies
3_clone.warning: ⚠️ CLONING IS YOUR LAST RESORT, NOT YOUR FIRST

5_WHEN_TO_CLONE_VS_BORROW.⚠️_performance_impact: Cloning can be 10-1000x slower than borrowing

ask_yourself: 1. Do I need to OWN this data? → Clone or move
2. Do I just need to READ it? → Borrow (&T)
3. Do I need to MODIFY it temporarily? → Mutable borrow (&mut T)
4. Is the borrow checker complaining? → DON'T clone yet, understand why first

valid_reasons: Storing data in multiple independent collections
Sending data to another thread (Arc<T> is better though)
Working around complex lifetime issues (after trying borrowing first)

anti_patterns: ❌ Cloning just to satisfy borrow checker without understanding
❌ Cloning in hot loops (lexer, parser main loops)
❌ Cloning when function only needs to read
❌ Cloning in return values when reference would work
when_clone_is_wrong.example_bad: fn process(data: String) { /* uses data.clone() everywhere */ }

specific_dixscript_guidance.lexer_tokens: DON'T clone tokens in main loop - use Vec<Token> and borrow
specific_dixscript_guidance.parser_state: DON'T clone parse state - use &mut references
specific_dixscript_guidance.error_collections: OK to clone individual errors when adding to collection
specific_dixscript_guidance.ast_nodes: DON'T clone during traversal - use &Node or &mut Node
specific_dixscript_guidance.string_literals: Use &str for reading, String for ownership

Copy.what: Implicit bitwise copy (like C# value types)
Copy.types: i32, f64, bool, char, and other primitives
Copy.behavior: let y = x; // x is COPIED, both valid

when_to_use.use_Copy_for: Small structs with only Copy fields (Point, Token metadata)
when_to_use.use_Clone_for: Types with heap data (String, Vec) or large structs
when_to_use.never_both_for: Types with heap allocations (can't be Copy)

🎯_NATIVE_RUST_COLLECTIONS_GUIDE.philosophy: Use native Rust collections + itertools for all collection operations

Vec<T>.when_to_use: Dynamic arrays, default choice for lists
Vec<T>.create: let mut vec = Vec::new(); or vec![1, 2, 3]

HashMap<K, V>.when_to_use: Key-value pairs with O(1) lookup, unordered

Join.c_sharp: list1.Join(list2, x => x.id, y => y.id, (x, y) => ...)

performance_tips.lazy_evaluation: Iterators are lazy - chain operations before .collect()
performance_tips.avoid_collect: Don't .collect() if you don't need to - keep it lazy
performance_tips.reuse_iterators: Can't reuse after .collect() - clone source if needed
performance_tips.parallel: Use rayon crate for parallel iteration on large datasets

🏗️_PORTING_STRATEGY.approach: Use native Rust collections + itertools instead of custom wrappers

rust_style_snake_case.what: All Rust code uses standard Rust naming
applies_to: All local variables (let token_type, let error_count)
rust_style_snake_case.reason: Standard Rust conventions, better tooling support

collections_usage.vec_t: For dynamic lists - replaces C# List<T>
collections_usage.hashmap_k_v: For dictionaries - replaces C# Dictionary<K, V>
collections_usage.hashset_t: For unique sets - replaces C# HashSet<T>
collections_usage.itertools: For LINQ operations - replaces C# LINQ methods

step_by_step_porting_workflow.2_identify_types: What types does it use? (List → Vec, Dictionary → HashMap)
step_by_step_porting_workflow.3_check_hot_path: Is this called in a loop? (Yes = native types, borrow heavily)
step_by_step_porting_workflow.5_port_methods: One method at a time, test each
step_by_step_porting_workflow.9_fix_errors: Read error messages carefully, they're helpful
step_by_step_porting_workflow.10_profile_if_slow: cargo flamegraph to find real bottlenecks
step_by_step_porting_workflow.11_iterate: Refine and optimize based on benchmarks

hot_paths.definition: Code executed thousands+ times per file (lexer loops, parser lookahead)

cold_paths.definition: Code executed once or rarely (setup, error reporting)
rules: ✅ Use String instead of &str for simplicity

avoid.repeated_cloning: for item in &items { let owned = item.clone(); } // ❌ Bad
avoid.string_concat_loop: for s in &strings { result = result + s; } // ❌ O(n²)

prefer.borrowing: for item in &items { process(item); } // ✅ Zero copy

cow_pattern.what: Clone-on-Write - borrows when possible, clones only when modified
cow_pattern.use_when: Data is USUALLY not modified, but SOMETIMES needs to be

value_moved_error.cause: Tried to use value after moving it
value_moved_error.fix_3_use_after:
println!("{}", s1);
let s2 = s1; // Use before move

cannot_borrow_as_mutable.error: cannot borrow as mutable because it is also borrowed as immutable
cannot_borrow_as_mutable.cause: Trying to mutate while immutable borrows exist
cannot_borrow_as_mutable.example_wrong:
let r1 = &data;
let r2 = &mut data; // ❌ Can't have both

cannot_move_out_of_borrowed.error: cannot move out of `*vec` which is behind a shared reference
cannot_move_out_of_borrowed.cause: Trying to take ownership from a borrow
